cases.statement: Two carriers in one Dutch family: mother (P1) and daughter (P2), both affected.

people.label: P1 (mother; D001)
people.key_phenotypes: childhood oral and genital ulcers; erosive RF-positive rheumatoid arthritis from age 18; type 1 diabetes, Hashimoto thyroiditis, pernicious anemia; antiphospholipid syndrome with vasculitis and arterial occlusion; IgA deficiency

quotes.quote: Her medical history included a childhood history of oral and genital ulcers.
At the age of 18, she was diagnosed with erosive rheumatoid arthritis, positive for rheumatoid factor (RF).
Later in life, she received diagnoses of pernicious anemia, Hashimoto’s disease, IgA deficiency, and insulin-dependent type 1 diabetes mellitus.
Consequently, the patient received a diagnosis of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) with both thrombosis and vasculitis.
This revealed a heterozygous NM_001270508.2: c.608T > G, p.(Leu203Arg) missense variant of TNFAIP3 in both patients

people.label: P2 (daughter; D002)
people.key_phenotypes: recurrent oral and genital ulcers since adolescence; immune thrombocytopenia; sterile neutrophilic folliculitis; symmetric polyarthritis; recurrent sinusitis with IgG2 subclass deficiency

quotes.quote: Patient 2, the daughter, presented at 29 years old with extensive hematomas due to severe thrombocytopenia (10 × 10E9/L), diagnosed as immune-mediated thrombocytopenia (ITP).
She had experienced recurring oral and genital ulcers since adolescence.
Examination revealed histologically confirmed sterile neutrophilic folliculitis and symmetric polyarthritis affecting the proximal interphalangeal joints.
Laboratory investigations indicated a mildly elevated CRP level (13–17 mg/L) and an IgG2 subclass deficiency (IgG2 0.19 g/L; reference range 1.50–6.40 g/L).
This revealed a heterozygous NM_001270508.2: c.608T > G, p.(Leu203Arg) missense variant of TNFAIP3 in both patients

phenotype_specificity.statement: Both have oro-genital ulcers plus mainly autoimmune disease, which the authors present as a predominantly autoimmune form of the disease. Exome sequencing with an inborn-errors-of-immunity panel found one other variant, TNFRSF13B p.(Cys104Arg), in the mother only, described as a known risk factor.

quotes.quote: as well as a heterozygous c.310T > C (p.Cys104Arg) variant of TNFRSF13B in the mother, a known risk factor that is present in 0.3%–0.5% of the normal population (GnomAD, v2.0.2).

Although this variant may contribute to the development of IgA deficiency and autoimmunity in the mother, its absence in the daughter suggests that it is not a critical modifier of the clinical phenotype.
Here, we describe a novel TNFAIP3 variant in a Dutch family, predominantly presenting with polyautoimmunity rather than autoinflammatory manifestations.

segregation.statement: Two affected carriers (mother and daughter): WES in the mother, Sanger segregation testing in the daughter. The mother's brother (deceased, 'rheumatism and thyroid disease') was not tested. No unaffected relatives were tested.

quotes.quote: Lastly, segregation analysis of the identified variants was performed in the daughter using standard Sanger sequencing.
Brother of P1 passed away at the age of 40, had been residing abroad, and had a known medical history of rheumatism and thyroid disease.

functional.statement: Patient PBMCs: lower A20/actin ratio by immunoblot after TNFα (P1 0.205, P2 0.218 vs mean of three healthy controls 0.802). HEK293T overexpression of a mutant construct: lower A20 (0.28 vs 1.18 wild type) with higher TRAF6 and phospho-IκBα. Patient cells also showed raised p65/IκBα, STAT1, mTOR and S6K phosphorylation and higher TNFα/IL-1β production. One of the three healthy controls had a post-TNFα ratio of 0.216, in the patients' range (see concerns). The authors note both patients were on immunosuppressive treatment.

quotes.quote: showed a significantly lower A20/actin ratio in patients compared to HCs, particularly after stimulation with TNFα (P1: 0.205; P2 0.218; L001 0.453 versus mean ratio HC:0.802, see Supplementary Table 1)

After stimulation, the A20/actin ratio was 1.18 for wild-type and 0.28 for mutant. Corresponding values for TRAF6 were 0.57 (wild-type) and 0.92 (mutant), and for phosphorylated IκBα were 0.13 (wild-type) and 0.18 (mutant).
In the constitutive state, we observed significantly higher levels of phosphorylated STAT1 in the patients, especially in T cells, monocytes and NK cells, when compared to HCs (Fig. 7A).
First, the analysis of PBMCs might have been suboptimal because of immunosuppressive treatment in the patients.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense variant (p.(Leu203Arg)) in the OTU domain. The paper describes the disease as caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants, and suggests this variant may reduce protein stability.

quotes.quote: Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene lead to A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20).
This variant is located in the OTU/deubiquitinylation domain (Fig. 1B).
the reduced abundance of the mutant protein, together with increased downstream signaling, suggests that the variant may affect protein stability

computational_predictions.statement: MetaRNN 0.94. Structural modelling puts a larger, positively charged residue into the hydrophobic core within the TRAF-binding region.

quotes.quote: consistent with a high MetaRNN score of 0.94, indicating a likely pathogenic variant effect

population_data_in_papers.statement: Not found in gnomAD or any other population database (paper's statement).

quotes.quote: The heterozygous c.608T > G (p.Leu203Arg) variant of TNFAIP3 was not found in the gnomAD browser nor in any other population database.
In conclusion, we have identified a novel pathogenic variant in TNFAIP3 associated with HA20, confirming its functional impact.

concerns: The mother (P1) also carries TNFRSF13B c.310T>C p.(Cys104Arg). The daughter does not.

In Supplementary Table 1, healthy control HC 3 has a post-TNFα A20/actin ratio of 0.216, about the same as P1 (0.205) and P2 (0.218). The healthy-control mean of 0.802 comes from three controls with a wide spread.
Functional assays used patient cells taken under immunosuppression (rituximab and TNF blockade) and a commercially bought mutant construct. The authors list the treatment effect as a limitation.
The two carriers are mother and daughter (the same family). They are not independent probands.
notes_for_panel: Supplementary Table 1 also includes L001, a separate carrier of c.1309del (see G-ha20-035), used as a control. De novo status is not reported: the mother's parents were not tested, and the daughter's carrier status follows the affected mother.
